summary: The same sign-in form as the reviewed self-hosted GitLab profile: one POST form (sign-in-form) at /users/sign_in. The software is public, but what gitlab.com serves was not observed, and its two-step sign-in can replace this layout per request.

sources.title: GitLab 19.4.2 sign-in form component (public mirror of the open-source edition)
This repository's test of the reviewed self-hosted GitLab form: the rendered form with its ids, field names and test ids
GitLab 19.4.2 password input component: name and test id are passed through, the type starts as password
GitLab 19.4.2 sign-in view: the field names are generated by the server form for the user model and handed to the component
GitLab 19.4.2 feature-test helper: signs in through the fields user_login and user_password, then user_otp_attempt
GitLab 19.4.2 feature flag two_step_sign_in: described as GitLab.com 2-step sign-in, a beta flag that is off by default
GitLab 19.4.2 sessions controller: the two-step flag is evaluated per request; a CAPTCHA can be required on login

GitLab Website Terms of Use, section 3 (responsibility of website visitors): no process, automated or otherwise, may retrieve, scrape or reproduce the presentation of the website. The reason the hosted page was not captured.

selectors.locator: line 40; source sign-in-form lines 16, 99-112 and 226-233 write the form id and the autocomplete value; source test-helper line 83 fills user_login
line 40; source sign-in-form lines 250-259; source password-input lines 86-88 and 113-118; source test-helper line 84 fills user_password

selectors.note: The passkey button is a submit button of a second form on the page, outside form#sign-in-form.

fixtures.note: The single-form layout (two-step sign-in off), with the passkey form beside it.

staysInteractive.note: The form has a CAPTCHA slot that the server turns on for some requests.
The verification code page has two layouts behind a flag; neither is pinned here.
The sign-in page initialises an email verification component (a code sent by email). When the site shows it was not read.
Provider buttons are rendered under the form, outside it.

unverified: What gitlab.com serves. The hosted page was not rendered (source website-terms), and the site runs ahead of releases with its own flag settings; the selectors are those of release 19.4.2.
Whether two-step sign-in is on for a given request on gitlab.com. With it on, the page first shows only the username field, and these steps stop as a layout mismatch with nothing typed.
Where two-step sign-in sends an account that lives on another cell, and whether that leaves the gitlab.com origin.
Additions of the hosted edition: the public mirror read here does not contain the ee directory, so anything gitlab.com adds to the sign-in page from there was not read.
neededFromUser: One sign-in on gitlab.com with this layout, or the signed-out sign-in page saved as "Webpage, Complete", to show which layout the account gets. Save any page signed out and with no password typed in; keep the "_files" folder beside the .html and both outside the repository: they can hold the account name.
schemaGaps: Two alternative layouts on one origin and path: the single form, and the two-step form in which the same button first checks the username and the password field is added to the form afterwards. A steps file can describe one of them; the single form was chosen because it is the release default.
notes: Labelled B although every selector is observed: the evidence covers the software, not the hosted deployment. robots.txt of gitlab.com allows /users/sign_in, but the website terms do not allow automated retrieval, so no capture was made.
